label: DRIFT (pass): the comment-hygiene convention holds across the advisor/hooks/relaunch cluster. Twelve lines carry a comment marker followed by an ephemeral label and zero are explanatory comments — seven are deliberate test-fixture string literals that exist to exercise the pre-commit linter on its own forbidden pattern ('// see ADR-12' at sk-code-post-edit-quality.test.cjs:69, codex-post-edit-quality.test.cjs:48, devin-post-edit-quality.test.cjs:50, post-edit-router.test.cjs:145 and three assertion strings) and five are JSONL transcript fixtures where a '//' inside prose preceded a specs/ mention. The closest case is compliant: scan.ts:40 names a directory shape (specs/<packet>), not a packet id. The AGENTS.md comment-hygiene rule and its pre-commit gate are enforced and clean here.

MISALIGNMENT: two module-header dialects across hook entry files, 84 versus 4, with no written canon and no enforcement. All 88 entry files under .skilled/hooks (excluding lib/, tests/, *.test.*) carry a box-drawing header, so none is headerless; but 84 identify themselves with '// MODULE:' (the reference form, dispatch/lib/dispatch-audit.mjs:2, followed by a single-rule box and a prose paragraph) and 4 use a double-line box with '// COMPONENT:' plus '// PURPOSE:' — dispatch/claude/dispatch-audit-posttooluse.mjs:3, dispatch/claude/dispatch-preflight-lint.mjs:3, dispatch/cursor/dispatch-preflight-lint.mjs:3 and post-edit-quality/claude/claude-posttooluse.cjs:3. Repo-wide the split is 2069 '// MODULE:' headers against 80 '// ║ COMPONENT:' headers, so MODULE is the de facto canon and COMPONENT the minority dialect. Neither marker is written down as a rule and nothing reads either: every MODULE hit outside .skilled/hooks is a source file carrying a header, never a tool parsing one. Nothing breaks today, which is why severity is P2; what would break after a fix is that anything grepping '^// MODULE:' for a module inventory silently drops those 4 files.

The sweep's own instrument is coarse in exactly one direction: the first rg pass returned 56 lines against the comment-filtered pass's 12, a 4.7x inflation driven entirely by string literals and JSONL payloads. Any automation of this check must anchor on comment syntax, and should be a TS parser rule rather than a regex.
Census figures for the header dialect: 88 hook entry files all headered, 84 MODULE, 4 COMPONENT; repo-wide 2069 MODULE versus 80 COMPONENT.
